summary: Lookout man on Fort Rock by 1914 and a station on the rim by 1919; the rock is now a public state natural area. No source describes the lookout site today.

access.note: Public parking near the south and southeast sides. Public access to the falcon nesting areas is closed February 15 to August 30 during brooding season.

visit.trail_note: The promontories of the wave-cut benches on the south and southeast sides are the most popular hiking destinations; a public parking area is near them.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A lookout man was on the rock in 1914, before the earliest report of a placed station (1919). The sources do not say whether the 1914 watch used a structure, so the build date stays open.

The Oregon Encyclopedia body text puts the mid-1920s lookout structure on the south bluff; its own 1921 photo caption puts a small lookout structure on the west promontory. The story reports the body text and notes the caption; the sources do not settle which is right.

notes_for_editor: Built date unknown: the 1914 item shows a lookout man on the rock; the 1919 item is the earliest report of a placed station; the 1920 and 1921 items are about staffing. The Oregon Encyclopedia body text puts the mid-1920s photograph on the south bluff, undated beyond that, but its 1921 photo caption places a small lookout structure on the west promontory; the story reports both and does not settle it. The benchmark 'until recently' suggests the marker is gone, but no source says what happened to the structure. The Cabin Lake (Fort Rock Ranger District headquarters, 1921-1945) article in The Bulletin, 2006, was read for context only and is not cited; it does not describe the lookout. Access level public rests on the Oregon Encyclopedia's public parking and falcon closure text. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the Forest Lookouts entry confirms the item dates (September 23, 1914; November 16, 1919; July 15, 1920; June 27, 1921).
